returnRules.title: Yellow fever certificate if you were in a risk country in the last 6 days
returnRules.detail: Travellers aged 9 months or older arriving from, or who stayed or transited outside the airport transit area in, one of the 42 countries on India's yellow fever list must hold a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate (international certificate, IHR 2005 Annex 6, issued by an authorised centre). It becomes valid 10 days after vaccination and is valid for life. Without a valid certificate you are quarantined until it becomes valid or until 6 days from the last possible exposure, whichever is first. Photocopies, scans and digital copies are not accepted. A medical exemption letter does not waive quarantine. Applies to Indian citizens too.

returnRules.title: Polio vaccination for arrivals from polio-affected countries
returnRules.detail: Per the MoHFW revised advisory (office order dated June 2024), anyone arriving in India with a passport of, or a travel history in the last year to, the 11 listed polio-affected countries needs a polio vaccine dose (OPV or IPV) at least 4 weeks before travel, with a certificate valid for one year. It applies to Indian nationals and NRIs from these countries too. Travellers without a certificate must receive OPV at the arrival airport. Indian nationals travelling to these countries need it for outbound travel as well.

returnRules.title: Customs: duty-free allowance and declaration
returnRules.detail: Baggage Rules 2026 (effective 2 Feb 2026) give an Indian resident returning by air or sea a general duty-free allowance of Rs 75,000 on articles (previously Rs 50,000). Allowances cannot be pooled between passengers. Above the allowance, duty applies and goods go through the red channel.

returnRules.title: Foreign currency declaration
returnRules.detail: Declare on a Currency Declaration Form if foreign currency notes exceed USD 5,000, or total foreign exchange (notes, banknotes, travellers cheques) exceeds USD 10,000, or equivalent.

returnRules.title: Indian rupees
returnRules.detail: Import of Indian currency is prohibited in general, but residents returning from abroad can bring up to Rs 25,000 (per an older Indian High Commission guide, current figure not re-confirmed on CBIC).

returnRules.title: Jewellery allowance
returnRules.detail: A resident or tourist of Indian origin who stayed abroad more than one year may bring jewellery up to 40 g (women) or 20 g (others) duty free in bona fide baggage.

polioSourceNote: India MoHFW revised polio advisory, office order dated June 2024 (text read by OCR). Endemic: Afghanistan, Pakistan. Circulating poliovirus: Cameroon, Nigeria, Malawi, Mozambique, Madagascar, Congo, DR Congo, Somalia, Syria. MoHFW says the list may be amended from time to time. WHO Polio IHR Emergency Committee 44th statement is dated 4 March 2026; it discussed Afghanistan, Angola, Germany, Laos, Namibia, Pakistan and Papua New Guinea, but the current full WHO list was not opened, so India's list may be out of date.
yellowFeverIndiaRule: MoHFW (Airport Health Organisation portal): passengers travelling to and from yellow fever risk countries must hold a valid certificate from an authorised centre, including those who leave the airport transit area in a risk country. Without a valid or mature certificate they are quarantined until the certificate becomes valid or for up to 6 days from last possible exposure, whichever is first. India's list has 42 countries, based on WHO list updated 3 Jan 2023. Africa: Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, DR Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Sudan, South Sudan, Togo, Uganda. Americas: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana (not in atlas), Guyana, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela. Not on India's list: Tanzania, Zambia, Rwanda, Eritrea, Sao Tome and Principe, Somalia. Source: https://www.ihpoe.mohfw.gov.in/vaccination.php and Indian missions' MoHFW guideline notices.

customs.dutyFreeAllowance: Rs 75,000 general free allowance for a resident returning by air or sea (Baggage Rules 2026, effective 2 Feb 2026). Used personal effects separate. Jewellery 40 g women or 20 g others after more than 1 year abroad. Alcohol and cigarette quantities (reported secondary as 2 litres and 100 cigarettes) UNVERIFIED on an official page.
customs.currencyLimits: Foreign currency: declare if notes exceed USD 5,000 or total including travellers cheques exceeds USD 10,000 (no upper cap). Indian rupees: up to Rs 25,000 for returning residents per older HCI guide, UNVERIFIED as current.
customs.declaration: Use the red channel if carrying dutiable goods above the allowance, prohibited or restricted items, or currency above the limits. Fill a Currency Declaration Form for foreign currency above the limits.
customs.prohibited: Per CBIC passenger guide: gold and silver other than ornaments (import), Indian and foreign currency above prescribed limits, satellite phones, drones, radio transmitters not approved for normal use. Also narcotics, weapons (general).

other: Indian passport holders do not need the e-Arrival Card; it is mandatory since 1 April 2026 for foreign nationals and OCI cardholders (reported by the Indian Embassy in Cairo post and US Embassy notice, Indian citizens exempt per secondary source trip.com). Source: https://in.usembassy.gov/indias-new-digital-arrival-system
Emigration Check Not Required (ECNR) and Air Suvidha style health declaration: not verified, nothing found about a current health declaration form for Indian arrivals.
